subject: Clarify scope/pricing before pen-test SOW finalization
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@attacklake.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-30 09:12 AM GMT
Subject: Clarify scope/pricing before pen-test SOW finalization

Nina —

Thanks for sending the initial SOW and estimate (received earlier this morning). Before we move forward I'd like to confirm a few technical and contractual points so we can avoid hours of back-and-forth during procurement. High-level asks below:

- Confirm exact assets in scope: our public web app (app.redwood.ai), API endpoints under api.redwood.ai, and two internal staging clusters (staging-1, staging-2). Is CI/CD pipeline testing included or considered a separate engagement?
- Test window: we're aiming for a production-safe red-team over two non-consecutive business days (4-6 hours each day). Your SOW mentions a 3-day window — can you map your tasks to the shortened window and note which tests would be deferred?
- Evidence & deliverables: we require raw findings (no redaction) for engineering, structured CSV export for ticketing, and a short executive summary for GTM. Please confirm delivery timelines.
- Data handling & retention: SOC2 controls are required. We need clarification on how long you retain evidence and whether you can store anything in our S3 (we'd prefer vendor-hosted with AES-256).
- Insurance & certs: please attach current cyber liability limits and proof of E&O.

Cc'ing Marissa (procurement lead), Karthik (AppSec) and Soojin (engineering owner) to flag anything I missed. If we can get a concise response to these items, procurement can turn the SOW in 48–72 hours.

Thanks,
Sean
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0199

Attachment: none in this message
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@attacklake.com>

Cc: Procurement <procure@attacklake.com>
Date: 2027-06-30 14:05 GMT
Subject: Re: Clarify scope/pricing before pen-test SOW finalization

Sean —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline below, and I'm attaching our SOW + price workbook for reference (AttackLake_SOW_v1.pdf, AL-quote-20270630.xlsx).

- Assets: public web app + API endpoints + the two staging clusters are all covered in the SOW. CI/CD pipeline testing is optional add-on (we flagged it as Phase II) — we can include a light CI check within the 2-day window but full CI/CD exploit attempts require additional time.
- Test window: we can compress to your 2 non-consecutive business days. The main trade-offs are fewer long-duration persistence simulations and reduced parallel red-team rotations; we'll annotate the SOW to call out deferred activities.
- Evidence: we will deliver: (a) raw evidence bundle (logs, screenshots, pcap where applicable), (b) prioritized findings CSV, and (c) 1-page exec summary within 5 business days after final retro. Detailed remediation guidance within 10 business days.
- Data handling: we retain evidence for 90 days by default; we can extend retention on request. We host evidence on encrypted storage (AES-256). We can also provide a short data handling addendum for SOC2 alignment.
- Insurance: attached certificate (in the SOW package) — cyber limits: $5M; E&O included.

We can provide a marked SOW with redlines across the scope items you called out by EOD tomorrow. If you're ready to proceed after that, we can route a DocuSign envelope for signatures.

Best,
Nina Patel
Client Solutions Director
AttackLake Security
ops@attacklake.com

Quick procurement notes after scanning the SOW:

- Please add a clause that any subcontractors must be pre-approved by Redwood with the same data handling terms.
- Payment terms: standard 30 days net; we'd prefer invoice milestones tied to delivery (50% kickoff, 50% on final report). If you require prepayment for reserved scheduling, call that out clearly.
- Cancellation/reschedule policy: we need 30-calendar-day notice for full refund on reserved window; shorter notice should have a partial credit policy.

Karthik / Soojin — can you confirm the minimum evidence package is sufficient for our SRE team? If you need specific logs/retention adjustments we should ask in the next round.

All —

Reviewed the updated SOW and the evidence checklist. Confirming this meets our minimums: raw logs, prioritized CSV, and the retainer for 90-day evidence retention are acceptable. Two small asks before procurement signs:

1) Can AttackLake include a sample CSV schema in the deliverables (column names + severity mapping)? That will speed triage.
2) For the staging clusters: we need confirmation you won't run destructive tests (no DB wipes, no production-like traffic flood) unless explicitly approved in writing. Add this as a non-destructive testing clause.

If we get those two items as a short update in the SOW or an addendum, procurement (Marissa) and sales (Sean) have the green light to sign the DocuSign envelope.
